Its data-sharing skill prescribes SDV as the technical control and packages it as a runnable procedure: `SingleTableMetadata`, the three single-table synthesizers, and both `run_diagnostic` and `evaluate_quality` appear in the executable pattern. The entry records SDV written into compliance guidance an agent can act on.

repo-zorai.summary: A persistent multi-agent execution platform whose daemon owns work, memory, approvals and long-running goals, with a bundled library of scientific skills. One of those skills is SDV, at `skills/scientific-skills/sdv/`, packaging `CTGANSynthesizer`, the multi-table `HMA1Synthesizer` and `sdv.evaluation` as procedures the agent can call. The skill targets a pre-1.0 API surface, so an agent following it would call names current SDV no longer exposes — a dating signal worth carrying for this class of entry.

site-sdv-dev.summary: Project landing site: library directory, community statistics and download counts, and the blog.

paper-machine-learning-synthetic-estimat.summary: This paper estimates carbon footprint in logistics processes by building a multidimensional synthetic dataset (transport distance, cargo weight, fuel type, traffic density, etc.) via domain-knowledge rules and statistical distributions, then comparing six ML algorithms (Linear Regression, Random Forest, Extra Trees, Gradient Boosting, SVR, XGBoost) for emission prediction, with XGBoost performing best. SDV's original DSAA paper (Patki et al., 2016) is cited only in passing as motivation for why synthetic data generation is preferred under data-access and privacy constraints, without any use of the SDV software itself.

paper-agentic-sabre-uncertainty-aware-20.summary: This paper proposes Agentic SABRE, an uncertainty-aware neuro-symbolic multi-agent framework for ransomware detection that fuses semantic and behavioural evidence via CNN agents with Monte Carlo Dropout, arbitrated by a decision-layer orchestrator with risk and uncertainty thresholds for triage. Evaluated on RDset and RanSMAP, it reports near-perfect AUC on semantic data and improved robustness under weak behavioural signals, with ablations quantifying each component's contribution. To address score-space class imbalance, the authors implement their own CTGAN-style generator/discriminator trained on the fused score vectors, conditioned on binary labels, to synthetically augment rare high-risk cases feeding the Decision Agent.
paper-agentic-sabre-uncertainty-aware-20.needs: Unclear whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was invoked on the score vectors or the authors built their own generator/discriminator following the CTGAN design; no library name, import, or constructor hyperparameters are given, so it is judged as a reimplementation (port) rather than api_user.

paper-beyond-synthetic-augmentation-grou.summary: This paper argues that group-aware threshold calibration -- setting separate decision thresholds per demographic group -- outperforms synthetic oversampling for handling class imbalance in tabular classification, evaluated on credit-default and related financial benchmarks across seven model families. The authors run CT-GAN (alongside SMOTE) as a comparison augmentation baseline, training it for 5 epochs and conditioning generation on the protected attribute, then show group-aware thresholding on the original data still outperforms thresholded CT-GAN-augmented data. CTGAN's conditional generation mechanism is used as one of the synthetic-augmentation baselines the paper's own thresholding approach is benchmarked against and ultimately shown to make redundant.
paper-beyond-synthetic-augmentation-grou.needs: Cannot tell from the text whether the authors used the official CTGAN/SDV package or their own reimplementation -- no import, package name, or constructor parameters are given, so api_user vs. port cannot be resolved.

paper-conditional-tabular-generative-adv.summary: This paper addresses data scarcity in chronic kidney disease (CKD) prediction by using CTGAN to augment a small UCI CKD dataset (400 samples) with varying ratios of synthetic-to-real data, then training several classifiers (AdaBoost, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, KNN) to show that CTGAN-based augmentation reduces overfitting and improves generalization. The authors explicitly instantiate the CTGANSynthesizer and SingleTableMetadata classes from the open-source SDV package and use SDV's built-in quality metrics (column shape similarity, column pair trends) to validate the synthetic data. SDV's CTGAN synthesizer and SingleTableMetadata/quality-report tooling are run directly as the core data-generation and evaluation engine underpinning the entire empirical study.

paper-copulas-deep-learning-review-2026.summary: A survey paper examining the two-way relationship between copulas and neural network / deep learning methods, covering how copulas can be built from generative deep models and how neural networks assist in copula goodness-of-fit and structure estimation. In discussing vine copula structure estimation, the authors describe Sun et al. (2019), which reformulates vine structure selection as a reinforcement-learning task solved with an LSTM. The SDV-family vine copula work is discussed in prose as a specific prior approach to vine structure estimation, not run or benchmarked by the authors.
paper-copulas-deep-learning-review-2026.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentences available, so depth of engagement with the SDV vine-copula work beyond the quoted description is uncertain.

paper-cost-effective-case-finding-2026.summary: This paper develops digital twin simulations to evaluate cost-effective case-finding strategies for cognitive impairment, using a simulated dataset generated with a generative adversarial network (GAN) deep learning approach. The GAN-based simulation underpins the digital twin population used to model case-finding scenarios. The CTGAN paper is cited only to support a passing description of GANs as the technology 'widely known in lay literature for creating convincing deep-fake data,' with no methodological detail tying the simulation specifically to the CTGAN implementation.
paper-cost-effective-case-finding-2026.needs: Full text not available; unclear whether the CTGAN library itself was used to generate the digital twin dataset or if the citation only supports a general lay description of GAN technology (deep-fake analogy).

paper-fenris-reproducible-benchmarking-f.summary: FENRIS is a reproducible benchmarking framework for federated synthetic tabular data generation in healthcare, built on Flower simulation with a plugin architecture for pluggable synthesizers, coordinators, partitioners, and evaluators, evaluated on three public clinical datasets against Fed-TGAN, FedTabDiff, and a FedSimpleGAN baseline across fidelity, utility, privacy, fairness, and scalability metrics. In its related-work discussion the authors position the SDV ecosystem and SDMetrics as mature non-federated synthetic-data and metric tooling that provides reusable fidelity/utility/diagnostic infrastructure but is not designed for federated execution or communication-cost measurement, distinguishing FENRIS's federated scope from it. The SDV library and SDMetrics are cited and characterized as prior non-federated tooling, not run within FENRIS's own experiments.

paper-integrated-multi-response-optimisa.summary: This paper develops a Taguchi–grey relational analysis–response surface methodology–ANN framework to optimise electrical discharge machining parameters (pulse-on time, pulse-off time, peak current) for EN8 steel, jointly targeting surface roughness, material removal rate, and tool wear ratio. A feed-forward ANN predictive model is trained on data augmented via CTGAN and benchmarked across multiple training algorithms to improve prediction accuracy. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run to generate augmented training data for the neural network component of the study.
paper-integrated-multi-response-optimisa.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was used directly or reimplemented, nor the exact role of conditional sampling.

paper-learning-majority-minority-transfo.summary: This paper proposes an oversampling framework for class-imbalanced classification that learns a parametric transformation mapping majority samples into the minority distribution, combining a maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) alignment objective with a triplet loss regularizer for boundary awareness. It is evaluated across 29 synthetic and real-world datasets against classical (SMOTE, ADASYN, MWMOTE) and generative (GAMO, MGVAE) oversampling baselines. CTGAN is included as one of the generative baselines, run to produce synthetic minority samples via its conditional GAN design and compared against the proposed method on AUROC, G-mean, F1-score, and MCC.

paper-multiomics-crlm-recurrence-2026.summary: Predicts early recurrence after resection of colorectal liver metastases by fusing radiomic, transcriptomic and clinical features in an FT-transformer, working from a single-centre cohort of 129 patients where the sample size is small relative to the dimensionality of RNA sequencing. CTGAN carries that constraint: it synthesizes additional gene-expression instances conditioned on recurrence outcome, generated inside each cross-validation training fold so the test fold stays untouched, and the authors name this augmentation as what makes the cohort tractable.

paper-probabilistic-causal-modelling-fac.summary: This paper analyzes survey and daily-diary data from nurses and social workers to uncover causal relationships among stress, anxiety, depression, and demographic/professional factors, combining reliability and correlation analysis with synthetic data generation and causal structure learning to compensate for a small sample size. To address data scarcity, the authors generate synthetic datasets using Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, and TVAE models trained across multiple epochs, then run causal discovery algorithms on the resulting synthetic data, citing the SDV dissertation as the source of these techniques. SDV's Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, and TVAE synthesizers are run directly as the data-generation stage whose output feeds the entire downstream causal-modelling experiment.

paper-qtabgan-hybrid-quantum-classical-2.summary: This paper introduces QTabGAN, a hybrid quantum-classical generative adversarial network that uses parameterized quantum circuits to learn complex tabular data distributions, mapping quantum outputs to tabular features via classical neural networks for privacy-constrained, data-scarce settings. It benchmarks QTabGAN against multiple classical tabular GAN baselines on classification and regression datasets, reporting improved accuracy, F1, correlation preservation, and JSD metrics. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of several baseline generators against which QTabGAN's synthetic data quality is quantitatively compared.
paper-qtabgan-hybrid-quantum-classical-2.needs: Evidence does not specify whether CTGAN/TVAE baselines were run via the sdv-dev package or the authors' own reimplementation; no import or constructor-parameter details given.

paper-rel8r-benchmarking-framework-tabul.summary: Introduces ReL8r, a proposed benchmarking framework for evaluating tabular data generators by constructing artificial relationships within datasets to test generator behavior. The work appears to compare multiple synthetic data generation methods within this new evaluation scheme. It cites the original SDV paper, but the metadata-only evidence does not show whether the SDV package or a synthesizer from it is actually run as part of the benchmark.

paper-small-imbalanced-noisy-datasets-20.summary: A systematic review of 126 articles addressing class imbalance, small sample size, and noise in clinical machine-learning datasets, surveying data-level, algorithm-level, and evaluation-metric strategies and proposing the InterLACE decision framework for selecting appropriate interventions. The review notes SMOTE-based oversampling as the most prevalent data-level technique among the surveyed literature. CTGAN is cited as one of the generative techniques discussed in this survey of methods for handling imperfect healthcare datasets.
paper-small-imbalanced-noisy-datasets-20.needs: Full text and the actual citing sentence for CTGAN were not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is merely listed among generative oversampling techniques or discussed in more depth.

paper-synthesize-adapt-steal-few-2026.summary: This paper proposes a few-shot, domain-adaptive model-stealing attack against black-box tabular ML models, combining synthetic query generation, a hybrid active-learning/adversarial query strategy, and a novel Relational Attention Corrector that enforces semantic validity. It is evaluated on an energy-sector intrusion-detection dataset (ERENO) and on Adult Income and Diabetes benchmarks, outperforming prior attacks and generator baselines like TabDDPM and GReaT. CTGAN is run as the core generator producing the synthetic data pool used to craft attack queries, and is benchmarked against diffusion- and LLM-based alternatives.
paper-synthesize-adapt-steal-few-2026.needs: Unclear whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev/ctgan package or reimplemented from scratch by the authors; no hyperparameter names or library import evidence given.

paper-theory-practice-map-inference-2026.summary: This paper develops two algorithms -- a message-passing solver (MPMAP) and a partition-and-optimize solver (PAMAP) -- for computing constrained MAP predictions over non-convex algebraic constraints and non-log-concave densities, evaluating them on synthetic and real-world benchmarks including a constrained imputation task on the House-Price dataset. For that imputation experiment they train a TVAE-style generative model, describing its own ELBO-style reconstruction/KL training objective 'extended to handle categorical data' rather than invoking the SDV package directly. TVAE, the deep generative model introduced alongside CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019), is reimplemented by the authors and used as the density model whose latent space their constrained MAP procedure is applied to.
paper-theory-practice-map-inference-2026.needs: Not fully certain whether the TVAE used was hand-built from scratch or adapted from an existing codebase; treated as a reimplementation (port) given the explicit description of their own training objective rather than a package call.

paper-robust-metric-evaluating-quality-2.summary: This paper introduces the Tabular Synthetic Data Score (TSDS), a bounded, interpretable framework for evaluating synthetic tabular data along three axes: fidelity, association, and authenticity, aimed at diagnosing issues like mode collapse and memorization in generative models. To validate TSDS across multiple UCI datasets, the authors generate synthetic data using three publicly available models from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) Python library, trained with SDV's default hyperparameters. CTGAN, TVAE, and the Gaussian Copula model are all run directly through the SDV library as the generative subjects whose outputs TSDS is used to score.

paper-framework-measurement-modeling-sea.summary: This study develops a probabilistic model and a CatBoost-based machine-learning model, trained on synthetic data augmented from field measurements, to estimate sea spray frequency for icing-risk assessment in marine operations. Field data were collected via the SPRICE sensor system at a fish farm in Northern Norway. In discussing data augmentation options, the authors mention CT-GAN alongside SMOTE, ADASYN, and WGAN as GAN-based methods explored for synthetic data generation, without detailing which was ultimately adopted.

paper-analytical-comparison-machine-lear.summary: This paper addresses automated test-case generation for satellite reaction-wheel passive rundown tests, training an SVM-RBF classifier guided by active learning to identify adequate test cases across three reaction-wheel profiles, and validating results with a lab wheel experiment. It compares this approach against several generative and classification methods for producing synthetic tabular test cases. A tabular Generative Adversarial Network (tGAN) is cited and employed as one of the competing generative methods against which the proposed SVM-RBF technique is evaluated.
paper-analytical-comparison-machine-lear.needs: Full text around the actual tGAN experiment/results section was not retrieved, only the introductory mention and reference list; unclear how thoroughly tGAN was run or compared.

paper-crest-counterfactual-realistic-exp.summary: This paper proposes CREST, a counterfactual-explanation method for tabular data that uses a conditional generative model to sample realistic, on-manifold counterfactual candidates, which are then filtered by prediction-flip success and ranked by proximity while enforcing feature immutability. It is evaluated against LIME-C and DiCE baselines on datasets such as Adult and German Credit, showing improved realism accuracy, proximity, and flip rate. CTGAN's conditional tabular GAN design (mode-specific normalization, conditional sampling) is cited and adopted as the basis for CREST's surrogate generative model, though it is unclear whether the SDV-dev package itself was run.

paper-distributed-generative-model-synth.summary: This paper proposes a distributed generative model framework for hierarchical IoT systems, supporting data generation across feature-related, label-related, and feature-label non-related scenarios with synchronous and asynchronous update mechanisms, validated on simulated, image, and tabular datasets. CTGAN and TGAN are only cited in passing: CTGAN's paper is referenced to support a remark about the difficulty of learning imbalanced data distributions, and TGAN is mentioned as the generator used in a prior work (Fed-TGAN) discussed in related work. Neither model is implemented or run by the authors, so SDV-family work is engaged only through citation.

paper-domain-aware-tabular-augmentation-.summary: This work proposes an LLM-based domain-aware tabular data augmentation method that encodes scientific constraints via policy generation, applied to an imbalanced geochemical rock classification dataset where closure constraints and correlations must be preserved. It outperforms SMOTE, Gaussian sampling, and no-augmentation baselines in accuracy and macro-F1. CTGAN is named only in a background sentence listing deep generative models (alongside TVAE and CTAB-GAN) used for tabular synthetic data generation, without being run or evaluated.

paper-enhancing-metabolic-syndrome-predi.summary: This paper evaluates machine learning models (XGBoost, Random Forest, TabNet) for predicting Metabolic Syndrome and introduces MetaBoost, a hybrid data-balancing framework that combines SMOTE, ADASYN, and CTGAN via weighted averaging to address class imbalance, followed by counterfactual analysis to identify key risk-shifting features like blood glucose and triglycerides. CTGAN is trained directly on the clinical dataset (for 100-300 epochs depending on the combination) both alone and jointly with SMOTE/ADASYN, and its accuracy/F1 results are reported and combined into the proposed hybrid method. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization approach to tabular generation is the concrete synthesizer run as one of several oversampling techniques, and it is also fused into the authors' novel MetaBoost balancing pipeline.

Based on the metadata alone, its methodological contribution appears to center on machine-learning modeling for a healthcare diagnostic task rather than on data synthesis itself. paper-genai-digital-twins-aided-2025.summary: This paper develops an anomaly-detection framework for wearable physiological data (heart rate, activity) aimed at early detection of infectious disease outbreaks, using a Wasserstein GAN to generate synthetic wearable data that augments training sets for a cokurtosis-based multivariate anomaly detector. The authors evaluate uncertainty in the synthetic data relative to real data and in anomaly-detection thresholds. CTGAN is only cited in a reference list as an example of GAN-based tabular data generation, with no evidence it was run.

paper-generative-adversarial-network-ima.summary: This paper proposes DPGAN-IT, a differentially private GAN that jointly generates image and tabular data with strong privacy guarantees, evaluated on CelebA (images+attributes) and a Brain Tumor dataset (images+clinical records). For the tabular modality it compares against TVAE, CTGAN and CTAB-GAN as non-DP baselines, and it evaluates synthetic tabular utility/privacy using metrics documented at docs.sdv.dev/sdmetrics. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE synthesizers are run as comparison baselines, and the SDMetrics component is used to compute the quality/privacy scores reported in the experiments.

paper-perai-privacy-enhancing-amp-2025.summary: This paper presents PERAI, a lifecycle-oriented framework from PrivaSapien that embeds privacy and governance controls across five stages of the enterprise AI pipeline, including privacy threat modeling, PETs, agentic red teaming, and runtime enforcement. Synthetic data generation is discussed as one of several Privacy-Enhancing Technologies used during model training and assessment to reduce memorization and leakage risks. paper-earthquake-magnitude-ctgan-2025.summary: Estimates earthquake magnitude from P-wave precursor features for early warning, where the Japanese catalogue is heavily skewed against the high-impact events that matter most. CTGAN learns the first-arrival characteristics and generates the missing strong-event records, so SDV addresses a class imbalance whose minority class is the one the system exists to catch.

paper-real-time-explainable-iot-2025.summary: This paper proposes an intrusion detection system (IDS) for IoT networks that combines a Conditional Tabular GAN with explainable AI methods (SHAP and LIME) to address class imbalance and lack of interpretability in cyber-attack detection. The system is evaluated on multiple intrusion datasets and deployed on a resource-constrained edge device (Jetson Nano) to demonstrate real-time applicability. CTGAN is used as the synthetic data generator to oversample minority attack classes, forming the core generative component of the proposed detection pipeline.

paper-synthetic-medicine-legal-ethical-2.summary: This short communication proposes a legal-ethical framework for evaluating synthetic patient data used in profiling, situating a three-part taxonomy of synthetic data (fully, partially, and hybrid synthetic) within EU regulatory instruments including the GDPR, AI Act, and Medical Devices Regulation. It analyzes profiling practices through the four biomedical ethics principles and calls for governance mechanisms and generation quality benchmarks. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in a reference list supporting a general claim that synthetic data can closely mirror real datasets, with no engagement with the SDV library or method.

paper-syntheto-pcos-fairness-aware-2025.summary: This paper proposes Syntheto-PCOS, a framework that uses generative data augmentation to address small, imbalanced clinical datasets for PCOS diagnosis, followed by Bayesian-optimized ensemble classifiers (RandomForest, LightGBM) and SHAP-based explainability. The augmented, balanced dataset drives a suite of five ML models, with LightGBM achieving an AUC of 0.893 and 68.8% recall. CTGAN is trained directly on the normalized clinical feature set for 300 epochs and its synthetic output is concatenated with real data to double the training cohort, making it the sole generator underpinning the entire empirical pipeline.

In their experiments the authors also use an implementation of tabular GAN, citing Xu et al.'s CTGAN paper, apparently as a comparison method to their diffusion approach. CTGAN is referenced only briefly as an existing tabular-data generation technique used in the experiments, without further description of how it was configured or its results.

paper-hybrid-feature-extraction-integrat.summary: This paper proposes a cloud-based malware detection system that combines hybrid feature extraction techniques with an integrated deep learning model to classify malicious software. The work targets improved detection accuracy and robustness in cloud computing environments. CTGAN is cited among the referenced works, but the manner of its use (e.g., for data augmentation or class balancing) cannot be determined from the available evidence.
paper-hybrid-feature-extraction-integrat.needs: Full text or abstract needed to determine whether CTGAN was actually run (e.g., for oversampling malware samples) or merely cited in passing; integration and importance are best guesses from metadata alone.

paper-identifying-distinctive-brain-regi.summary: This paper conducts a quantitative neuroimaging meta-analysis using activation likelihood estimation to identify brain regions associated with branded versus unbranded food choices, and proposes a novel multi-coordinate pattern analysis (MCPA) combined with sparse PLS discriminant analysis to detect distinctive brain regions from coordinate-based foci data. It finds the ventral medial prefrontal cortex active for both food types, while the lingual gyrus and parahippocampal gyrus are distinctively activated for branded foods. CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) is cited only in passing, alongside SMOTE, as an example of a promising data augmentation method, but is neither used nor engaged with in the study.

paper-improvement-machine-learning-model.summary: This paper addresses the scarcity of real-world ship design data by generating synthetic container-ship main-particulars data points and training multilayer perceptron regressors on mixtures of original and synthetic data, showing improved R² and MAPE performance over models trained on original data alone. The synthetic data generation is performed using GaussianCopula, explicitly identified as being from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), which models the joint distribution of the ship particulars via copulas assuming (optionally non-normal) marginal distributions. SDV's GaussianCopula synthesizer is run directly as the sole generator underpinning the entire empirical study.

paper-db-unlearning-2024.summary: First study of data deletion, rather than insertion, in neural-network-backed database components, comparing retraining, fine-tuning, gradient ascent, NegGrad+, SCRUB and SISA across cardinality estimation, approximate query processing, data generation and classification, and proposing model-internal metrics alongside downstream ones. TVAE, released with CTGAN, is the data-generation model being unlearned; its forget quality is measured by the accuracy of an XGBoost classifier trained on samples it generates after deletion, following the protocol of the CTGAN paper.

paper-prediction-classification-phenol-c.summary: This agronomy study builds a stacking ensemble model to predict and classify total phenol content in the medicinal plant Cnidium officinale Makino under different climate-change scenarios, addressing severe class imbalance in a small field-collected dataset. To overcome the imbalance, the authors used the TVAE algorithm to generate 27,000 augmented records, validating similarity to the original data via cosine, correlation and Jensen-Shannon measures before feeding the augmented set into their regression and classification pipeline. TVAE, the variational-autoencoder synthesizer from the SDV/CTGAN family, is run directly as the data-augmentation generator underpinning the whole empirical pipeline.
paper-prediction-classification-phenol-c.needs: Not explicit whether TVAE was run via the SDV package or a separate/custom implementation; cited to the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper rather than an SDV package reference, so library provenance is inferred, not confirmed.

paper-sync2s-efficient-method-synthesizi.summary: This paper proposes SynC2S, a synthetic tabular data generation method that combines a learnable pre-processing technique (C2Smap) for continuous variables with a hierarchical conditional generative model (HCIWAE) for imbalanced categorical data. It benchmarks SynC2S against numerous competing generators on statistical similarity, ML efficacy, and over-sampling tasks. TVAE, CTGAN, and CopulaGAN are implemented using SDV's publicly available GitHub code and run as three of several baseline synthesizers throughout the experiments.
paper-sync2s-efficient-method-synthesizi.needs: Full text not obtained; author affiliations and finer detail on how SDV models were configured are unknown from abstract/citing sentences alone.

paper-hybrid-architecture-conditional-ta.summary: This paper proposes CTGAN-Conv1D, a hybrid architecture for IoT intrusion detection that addresses class imbalance in attack datasets by generating synthetic minority-class samples. The authors replace CTGAN's generator with a 1D convolutional neural network and evaluate the resulting synthetic data's ability to improve Random Forest classification on the UNSW-NB15 dataset, comparing against unmodified CTGAN and no augmentation. SDV's CTGAN, including its mode-specific normalization approach, is directly modified at the architecture level -- its generator is replaced -- to create the new CTGAN-Conv1D model.
paper-hybrid-architecture-conditional-ta.needs: Unclear whether the modification started from the sdv-dev ctgan package source or an independent reimplementation; treated as derivative_work regardless since CTGAN's own generator architecture is what is altered.

paper-applying-augmentation-technique-bl.summary: This paper addresses limited and imbalanced datasets in predicting blast-induced overbreak in tunnel excavation, a common problem in rock engineering/mining. It applies a data augmentation technique to expand and balance the training data before building predictive models for overbreak. The evidence indicates the work cites the CTGAN and SDV papers, suggesting CTGAN was used as the generator for synthetic sample augmentation, though full methodological detail is not available.
paper-applying-augmentation-technique-bl.needs: Full text or citing sentences needed to confirm whether CTGAN was run directly (api_user) or only cited as related work (citation_only), and whether SDV's library or a reimplementation was used.

paper-assessing-utility-synthetic-densit.summary: This paper proposes a density-ratio-estimation framework for evaluating the utility of synthetic data, offering a unified, interpretable measure that bridges fit-for-purpose and global utility metrics and yields point-level and analysis-specific diagnostics. It targets the broader problem of iteratively assessing synthetic data quality when disseminating research data to reduce disclosure risk. The work cites CTGAN and the SDV framework as examples of synthetic data generation approaches relevant to this evaluation problem.
paper-assessing-utility-synthetic-densit.needs: Full text needed to confirm whether CTGAN/SDV are actually run in the empirical examples or only cited as background examples of synthetic data generators.

paper-conditional-generators-limit-order.summary: This paper studies a conditional GAN (LOBGAN, from Coletta et al. 2022) used to simulate limit order book dynamics for trading agent evaluation, applying adversarial-attack techniques to probe the model's feature dependence and then using these insights to improve its realism and robustness. The main experiments run this LOB-specific CGAN, not any SDV component. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) is cited only in passing as prior work applying GANs to tabular data, with no use in the paper's experiments.

paper-generation-synthetic-improve-secur.summary: This paper introduces CyberSyn, a novel algorithm for generating synthetic process and network data sets to improve machine-learning-based security monitoring in cyber-physical production systems, evaluating it via data quality metrics across two industrial scenarios (process manufacturing and industrial communication networks). The authors explicitly base their implementation for synthetic data generation and evaluation on the Python library Synthetic Data Vault, and derive their quality metrics from the SDV paper by Patki, Wedge and Veeramachaneni. SDV is cited as the foundation for both the generation approach and the evaluation metrics adopted, though the paper describes its own CyberSyn algorithm using a generative adversarial network approach rather than clearly running SDV's own synthesizer code.
paper-generation-synthetic-improve-secur.needs: Unclear whether SDV's own synthesizer (e.g. GaussianCopula/CTGAN) is invoked directly via the library, or only its quality metrics/framework are reused while CyberSyn's own GAN-based generator produces the data; integration marked unclear pending clarification.

paper-cramers-v-tabular-gan-2023.summary: Starts from a known weakness of CTGAN, that it does not preserve dependencies between categorical columns, and asks whether making that dependency structure explicit during training fixes it. Cramer's V, the natural correlation measure for pairs of categorical variables, is introduced into training two ways: as a penalty term added to the generator's loss, and by extending the critic's input with a Cramer's V matrix computed per batch so it can detect categorical dependencies directly. On three benchmark datasets the modified model raises the averaged accuracy of supervised models trained on its output by 11 percent over the unmodified CTGAN, and the paper reports the effect on integrity and contingency similarity. The modification is made inside CTGAN's own loss and critic rather than around a frozen model, and CTGAN is both the substrate and the comparison, so this is a derivative of CTGAN even though the resulting model is never given a name of its own.

paper-poisoning-network-flow-classifiers.summary: This paper studies clean-label backdoor poisoning attacks against machine-learning classifiers used for network traffic flow analysis, introducing trigger-crafting strategies including one based on generative Bayesian network models to make triggers stealthy. The empirical work focuses on Zeek-derived traffic features and evaluates attack feasibility and detectability across multiple classification tasks. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) is cited only in the reference list, with no evidence it was run or engaged with in the body text.
paper-poisoning-network-flow-classifiers.needs: No body-text sentence citing CTGAN was found in the provided evidence beyond the bibliography; confirm whether an in-text citation exists elsewhere in the paper.

paper-tabular-synthesis-generative-adver.summary: This VLDB Journal article presents a unified GAN-based framework for tabular data synthesis, defining a design space of neural architectures, training strategies, and normalization techniques, and reporting extensive experiments comparing GAN-based methods against conventional privacy-preserving data publishing approaches. The authors adopt CTGAN's GMM-based mode-specific normalization and its conditional-vector mechanism as design choices within their own framework rather than running the SDV library itself, while the original Synthetic Data Vault paper appears only in the reference list with no further discussion in the body text. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional sampling design are described and reimplemented in the authors' own prose as one design option among many, and SDV (Patki et al. 2016) is cited only bibliographically.
paper-tabular-synthesis-generative-adver.needs: Reference [73] is inferred to be the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper based on described technique (condition vector, GMM normalization), but the excerpt of the reference list provided does not show entry 73 explicitly; this inference could not be independently confirmed from the given evidence.

paper-materials-discovery-generative-202.summary: Argues that advanced materials gate progress across aeronautics, automotive and construction, and that candidate discovery is bounded by how few characterised compounds exist. A CTGAN is developed per material class to generate novel synthetic compounds, so SDV's conditional architecture is used to propose candidates rather than to protect data.

paper-fully-observable-markov-decision-2.summary: This paper proposes a reinforcement-learning framework for line-of-sight estimation and traffic scheduling across multiple satellite links in integrated 6G non-terrestrial networks, using generative models to convert a partially observable MDP into a fully observable one by synthesizing channel states for links the agent has not yet accessed. The authors explicitly train and evaluate CTGAN and TVAE models, stating these 'belong to the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) package,' comparing synthetic and real channel-state distributions via KS-test and KL-divergence and feeding the synthetic states directly into the RL agent's observations. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE synthesizers are run as the core generators producing the synthetic channel data that the whole FOMDP conversion and RL convergence results depend on.

paper-assessing-deep-generative-models-2.summary: This paper compares three deep generative approaches -- TimeGAN, DoppleGANger, and the Probabilistic Auto-Regressive (PAR) model -- for producing synthetic time-series wireless network traffic data under varying levels of data scarcity, and evaluates downstream forecasting performance of a gradient boosting regressor trained on real, synthetic, or mixed data. PAR, described as part of the Synthetic Data Vault collection, is trained and sampled to generate synthetic traffic data that is evaluated qualitatively (histograms) and quantitatively alongside the GAN-based models, while CTGAN is only named in passing as an example tabular generative model without being run. SDV's PAR sequential synthesizer is run as one of three generative models compared in the empirical study.
paper-assessing-deep-generative-models-2.needs: CTGAN is mentioned once as background ('One model used to generate tabular data is the CTGAN [34]') but is not run in this paper's experiments; treated as citation_only aside within an otherwise api_user record centered on PAR.

paper-design-concrete-incorporating-micr.summary: This work develops a machine learning framework combining generative adversarial networks with other models to design concrete mixtures containing microencapsulated phase change materials for clean-energy applications. It appears to use GAN-based synthetic data generation to augment or model a limited experimental dataset for concrete property prediction. The paper cites the original TGAN (2018) paper, but no full text is available to confirm whether the SDV-family TGAN model itself was run or only cited as background on GAN-based tabular data generation.
paper-design-concrete-incorporating-micr.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN/SDV code was actually run for data generation or only cited as related work on GAN-based synthesis.

paper-gan-approaches-generating-structur.summary: This paper compares five GAN variants (GAN, CGAN, CTGAN, CopulaGAN, WGAN-GP) for generating synthetic tabular medical data to augment small breast-cancer datasets and improve binary classifier accuracy. The authors implement custom GAN/CGAN and WGAN-GP models but explicitly state they 'utilized the available implementations of CTGANs and CopulaGANs from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV)' as two of the five generators evaluated across multiple sampling strategies and dataset sizes. SDV's CTGAN and CopulaGAN thus serve as two of several synthesizers run directly through the SDV library in the empirical comparison.

paper-intrusion-detection-model-updates-.summary: This paper proposes a two-step model update procedure for network intrusion detection: first augmenting sampled network traffic with a GAN, then applying transfer learning to update the classifier with reduced labeling and computational cost. Evaluated on a large one-year network traffic dataset, the approach improves true-positive rates while cutting update costs. The GAN-based augmentation step relies on CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, as the generator producing the augmented training data.
paper-intrusion-detection-model-updates-.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev/ctgan package or reimplemented, nor whether the conditional vector was specifically leveraged.

paper-validating-membership-disclosure-m.summary: This paper develops and validates a corrected parametrization for the widely-used partitioning method that estimates membership disclosure risk (F1 score) of synthetic data, comparing estimated risk against ground-truth simulated attacks across four population health datasets and demonstrating the approach on seven clinical trial datasets. Two generative methods are evaluated as synthesis engines: sequential decision-tree synthesis and a GAN-based method. CTGAN is run as one of the two generative models used to produce the synthetic datasets on which the membership disclosure metric is tested and benchmarked across varying training sample sizes (5k/15k/25k).
paper-validating-membership-disclosure-m.needs: Affiliations for co-authors Mosquera and Fang are not stated in the provided evidence.

paper-event-mining-driven-context-2021.summary: This paper proposes a personal food model that incorporates causal contextual factors into food preference modeling, using an event mining approach on simulated food event data to uncover hidden preferences. The authors build their own food event simulator rather than using an existing synthetic data tool. The original SDV paper (Patki et al. 2016) is listed only in the bibliography, with no evidence it was used in the work.
paper-event-mining-driven-context-2021.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV is used, described, or merely cited in reference list.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-au.summary: This paper investigates GAN-based synthetic data augmentation for credit card fraud detection under class imbalance, examining how customer credit-quality distributions affect the benefits of augmentation and of transferring synthetic data between cooperating financial institutions. The empirical work centers on a custom GAN rather than any SDV tool. SDV's vine copula synthesizer (Sun et al. 2019) is only cited in passing as one of several prior synthetic-data generation methods in a literature-review sentence.
paper-generative-adversarial-networks-au.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV's vine copula method is discussed further beyond this literature-review sentence.

paper-improving-gan-inverse-cumulative-2.summary: This paper proposes a GAN-based method for tabular data synthesis that uses inverse cumulative distribution function transformations to better handle mixed continuous and categorical data types. It contributes an improved normalization/transformation approach for GAN training on tabular data, targeting issues like non-Gaussian and multimodal distributions. The paper cites the original SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) 2016 paper, likely as related work on synthetic data generation.
paper-improving-gan-inverse-cumulative-2.needs: Full text not obtained; only metadata available, so citation context and depth of engagement with SDV could not be verified.

paper-analysis-transferability-robustnes.summary: This paper investigates the transferability and robustness of generative adversarial networks that were evolved to approximate Pareto sets in multi-objective optimization problems, evaluating how well such evolved GAN models generalize across related problem instances. It sits in the evolutionary computation and generative modeling literature rather than the tabular-data-synthesis domain. The work cites the vine copula paper associated with the SDV/copulas family, apparently as a related statistical modeling reference rather than as a method it runs or benchmarks.
paper-analysis-transferability-robustnes.needs: No abstract, citing sentence, or full text was available; cannot confirm whether the vine copula work is engaged with beyond a bare citation or whether it relates to any SDV component's actual use.

paper-deep-generative-modeling-network-2.summary: A RAND Corporation report that surveys deep learning methods for network data and develops a new generative framework for large social contact networks used in epidemiological microsimulation and agent-based policy modeling, comparing these neural approaches against Exponential Random Graph Models. To generate node attribute data (tabular features like household demographics) for the NDSSL social contact network, the authors train a CTGAN model and compare the resulting synthetic feature distributions against the real dataset. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is run as the generator for the tabular node-attribute component of their network generation pipeline.

paper-generating-synthetic-finance-2020.summary: An introductory/position paper from J.P. Morgan AI Research surveying the challenges of generating synthetic data for financial services, focused on realism, similarity metrics, and privacy constraints, illustrated with two financial dataset examples. In its related-work discussion of tabular generative models the paper describes the Synthetic Data Vault's JSON-specified synthetic database approach and characterizes CT-GAN (and T-VAE) as the state-of-the-art conditional GAN architecture with mode-specific encoding for discrete and multi-modal continuous columns, noting it lacks privacy guarantees. Neither SDV nor CTGAN/TVAE is run in the paper's own experiments; both are cited and discussed only as prior art.
paper-generating-synthetic-finance-2020.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentences seen, so it is unclear whether SDV or CTGAN are discussed further or run anywhere in the body of this survey paper.

paper-stabilization-dataset-matrix-form-.summary: This paper studies methods for canonicalizing (stabilizing) the row/column order of classification dataset matrices so that convolutional-network-based generative models, specifically conditional GANs, can be applied to meta-learning problems of dataset generation and algorithm selection. The authors propose and evaluate several stabilization transformations and test them experimentally on dataset generation tasks. CTGAN (Xu et al.) appears only in the reference list as a citation for prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, with no use in the paper's own experiments.
paper-stabilization-dataset-matrix-form-.needs: Full text and abstract were not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run, adapted, or merely cited in the reference list.

paper-method-real-time-cfd-2018.summary: This paper develops a real-time computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling framework for natural ventilation control in buildings, using real-time sensor data as boundary conditions and data assimilation for self-calibration. The proof of concept is demonstrated with a synthetic case-study dataset rather than SDV-generated data. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in passing to support the general notion of using synthetic data for proof of concept, with no SDV component actually run.

preprint-enhancing-diversity-feasibility.summary: This paper proposes a joint generative approach for synthesizing agent-based-model populations from multiple data sources, using a Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty and a novel inverse gradient penalty regularization term to improve diversity and feasibility while addressing sampling and structural zeros. It surveys prior deep generative approaches to tabular/population synthesis, including a comparison table of GAN-based methods and their capabilities. TGAN is cited and described as one of the earlier tabular-data GAN models in this related-work discussion, but it is not run or benchmarked by the authors.

preprint-machine-learning-models-estimat.summary: This preprint develops and evaluates machine-learning counterfactual outcome models to construct a virtual control arm for a single-arm pediatric Crohn's disease study, comparing infliximab- versus adalimumab-treated patients against a propensity-score-matched reference. Five ML models (including LGBM, TabPFN, XGBoost) are trained with and without synthetic-data augmentation, where the augmentation records are generated by four generative methods -- adversarial random forest, Bayesian networks, CTGAN, and TVAE -- implemented through the authors' own 'pysdg' adaptation of the Synthcity package rather than the sdv-dev library itself. CTGAN and TVAE, both attributed to the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, are run as two of several data-augmentation generators whose outputs feed the counterfactual prediction pipeline.
preprint-machine-learning-models-estimat.needs: Unclear whether Synthcity's CTGAN/TVAE implementation used by the authors' 'pysdg' wrapper derives from the sdv-dev package or is an independent reimplementation; integration marked 'inherited' pending clarification.

preprint-quality-degradation-attack-synt.summary: This paper formalizes a threat model for insider 'quality degradation' attacks on synthetic data pipelines, where an adversary with access to the real dataset or generation process (e.g., data owner or synthetic data provider) manipulates inputs via label flipping or feature-importance-based interventions to degrade downstream utility and increase statistical divergence of the released synthetic data. It empirically evaluates these attacks across three generative models for tabular data. CTGAN and TVAE are run using their official implementations and default hyperparameters as provided by the SDV library, serving as two of the generators whose synthetic output is degraded and measured in the study.

preprint-context-bias-propagation-llm-20.summary: This paper studies how statistical biases present in in-context examples propagate into LLM-generated synthetic tabular data, showing that even mild biases in the demonstrations cause global distributional distortions and downstream fairness harms, and it further introduces an adversarial prompt-injection attack along with mitigation strategies based on preprocessing the in-context examples. As non-LLM baselines for comparison, the authors generate synthetic tabular data with classical tabular generators including TVAE and CTGAN. CTGAN and TVAE are run as one set of several baseline synthesizers benchmarked against the LLM-based in-context generation approach.
preprint-context-bias-propagation-llm-20.needs: Whether TVAE/CTGAN were run via the sdv-dev package specifically or a third-party reimplementation is not stated; only the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper is cited.

preprint-synthetic-weapon-against-androi.summary: This paper proposes MalSynGen, a conditional GAN-based methodology for generating synthetic tabular Android malware feature data to address scarcity and obsolescence of labeled malware samples for classifier training. The authors evaluate MalSynGen's fidelity, utility (TSTR/TRTS), and efficiency across multiple malware datasets (Drebin, Androcrawl, Kronodroid, Adroit). CTGAN, described as 'SDV's CTGAN', is run as a direct comparison baseline with matched hyperparameters, and MalSynGen is shown to outperform it on utility metrics across datasets.
preprint-synthetic-weapon-against-androi.needs: Unclear whether the SDV-dev package itself was invoked or the authors used the original CTGAN implementation from Xu et al.; evidence only labels it 'SDV's CTGAN' without package/import details.

preprint-time-tabpfn-integrated-multimod.summary: This paper proposes TIME, a multimodal framework that uses the frozen tabular foundation model TabPFN as an encoder to generate embeddings robust to missing data, fused with pretrained vision backbones for tabular-image learning tasks including medical applications. It evaluates fusion strategies across natural and medical datasets and shows improved performance over baselines. CTGAN is cited only as an example of prior generative modeling work for tabular data, with no code run or results reported.

paper-tabtreeformer-hybrid-2025.summary: Argues that transformers applied to tables lack the inductive biases that make tree ensembles effective on them, and answers with a hybrid in which a tree model supplies leaf-index prompts to the transformer while a dual-quantization tokenizer, K-means for modes and quantiles for precision, shortens sequences and shrinks the vocabulary, reaching competitive utility at a fraction of the model size. CTGAN is the acknowledged source of the multimodal-decomposition idea the tokenizer replaces and of the conditional generation the paper extends from single columns to clusters, but it is not among the eight generators run, where CTAB-GAN+ stands in for the GAN family.

preprint-withdrawn-hybrid-fuzzy-logic-20.summary: A withdrawn preprint proposing a hybrid fuzzy-logic and logistic-regression model with recursive feature elimination for predicting Type 2 diabetes mellitus in adults aged 35-45, intended as a clinical decision-support tool. The authors withdrew the manuscript due to errors in experimental design affecting result integrity, so no findings should be relied upon. In preprocessing, CTGAN is applied alongside SMOTE to synthetically augment the minority class and address class imbalance and overfitting in the diabetes dataset.
preprint-withdrawn-hybrid-fuzzy-logic-20.needs: Paper is withdrawn and only abstract-level withdrawal statement plus citing sentences were available; full text not obtained, so exact role/parameters of CTGAN could not be verified.

preprint-llm-mixer-multiscale-mixing-202.summary: This paper proposes LLM-Mixer, a time-series forecasting framework that decomposes input series into multiple temporal resolutions and feeds them to a frozen pre-trained LLM guided by a textual prompt, showing competitive accuracy across long- and short-term multivariate and univariate benchmarks. For an ablation analyzing how the number of downsampling levels affects learning dynamics (via Neural Tangent Kernel distance), the authors generate synthetic multivariate time series data. DeepEcho (cited as Patki et al., 2016) is run as the generator producing this synthetic multivariate data for the NTK ablation study.
preprint-llm-mixer-multiscale-mixing-202.needs: The paper cites DeepEcho to Patki et al. 2016 (the SDV/DSAA paper), which is a mis-citation since DeepEcho was introduced separately; recorded as given, not corrected.

preprint-proximal-policy-optimization-en.summary: This paper proposes P-TA, a method that fine-tunes an LLM as a GAN generator via proximal policy optimization to synthesize higher-quality tabular data for data augmentation, evaluated on three real-world tabular datasets (Travel, Adult Income, HELOC). The authors compare their approach against TVAE, CopulaGAN, and CTGAN as baseline tabular generators, reporting their accuracy and discriminator-based fidelity scores across all datasets. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN are run as baseline generators against which the proposed LLM+PPO method is benchmarked.

preprint-synhing-synthetic-heterogeneous.summary: This paper proposes SynHING, a framework for generating synthetic heterogeneous information networks (HINs) by identifying motifs from a target HIN and using bottom-up intra- and inter-cluster merge modules with post-pruning, providing ground-truth motifs to benchmark GNN explainer models. The work targets the scarcity of public HIN datasets and evaluation standards for graph explanation methods. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, with no engagement in the body text.

paper-tabdiff-2024.summary: Builds a joint continuous-time diffusion process that handles a table's numerical and categorical columns in one transformer-parameterized model, giving each feature its own learnable noise schedule so that columns with very different marginal shapes are not forced onto a shared corruption rate, and adds a mixed-type stochastic sampler that restarts the forward process at each denoising step to correct accumulated decoding error plus classifier-free guidance for imputing missing columns. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE representatives among the eight compared generators, reported across shape, trend, precision-recall and downstream columns on seven datasets.

preprint-transfer-learning-model-indoor-.summary: This preprint proposes a transfer learning model to predict indoor personal thermal comfort in tropical regions, using a case study from West Bengal, India. No further methodological detail is available from the evidence provided. It cites the CTGAN paper, but the nature of that citation (e.g., data augmentation for limited comfort survey data) cannot be determined from the metadata alone.
preprint-transfer-learning-model-indoor-.needs: Full text or abstract needed to determine whether CTGAN is actually run (e.g., for data augmentation of thermal comfort survey data) or merely cited in passing.

preprint-watermarking-generative-tabular.summary: This paper proposes a statistical watermarking mechanism for synthetic tabular data, embedding signals via strategic binning of continuous features and detecting them through a hypothesis-testing framework that requires only a continuous underlying density. It demonstrates theoretical guarantees on fidelity and robustness to additive noise attacks, validated empirically on six real-world datasets. TVAE, from the CTGAN paper, is run as one of three tabular data generators (alongside CTABGAN and TabDDPM) whose synthetic outputs are watermarked and evaluated for fidelity and ML utility.
preprint-watermarking-generative-tabular.needs: Evidence does not explicitly confirm whether the official SDV/CTGAN package's TVAE implementation was used versus a reimplementation; classified as api_user based on typical usage but not directly verifiable from text.

preprint-medical-records-condensation-ro.summary: This preprint proposes dataset condensation (DC) as a technique to democratise healthcare data by compressing electronic health records into small, statistically representative synthetic datasets that irreversibly obscure individual-level sensitive information while retaining enough signal to train deep neural networks. The authors validate the approach on three healthcare datasets with different data types (e.g., mortality prediction, COVID-19 diagnosis). CTGAN is only cited in the reference list as an example of prior generative-model work, with no experiments run against it.
preprint-medical-records-condensation-ro.needs: Full body text does not show any in-text engagement with CTGAN beyond the reference list entry; cannot confirm if it is discussed elsewhere in the paper's related-work section.

preprint-privacy-measurement-tabular-syn.summary: This paper surveys and codifies technical frameworks for quantifying the degree of individual privacy protection afforded by synthetic tabular data, covering both formal privacy guarantees and empirical attack-based assessment methods. It aims to raise interdisciplinary awareness and help synthetic-data researchers make informed modeling and evaluation choices, without proposing or running a generator itself. CTGAN and TGAN are named only in an undifferentiated citation group for GAN-based generators, never engaged with individually or run.

preprint-stunt-few-shot-tabular-2023.summary: This paper proposes STUNT, a meta-learning framework for few-shot tabular classification that self-generates diverse pseudo-tasks from unlabeled tabular data by clustering randomly selected columns, and introduces an unsupervised validation scheme for hyperparameter search. It is evaluated against self-supervised and unsupervised meta-learning baselines on multiple tabular benchmarks, showing significant performance gains. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of a sophisticated generative model that is cumbersome to train on tabular data, with no experiments run using it.

preprint-tsgm-flexible-framework-generat.summary: This paper introduces TSGM, an open-source, extensible Python framework for generating and evaluating synthetic time series data, supporting generative, probabilistic, and simulator-based methods along with multi-angle quality evaluation (similarity, downstream effectiveness, privacy, fairness, etc.). In its related-work comparison, the authors describe DeepEcho, part of the SDV ecosystem, as implementing basic GAN and probabilistic autoregressive models for time series, and place it in a feature-comparison table against TSGM and other frameworks. DeepEcho's PAR-style sequential model is discussed and compared on capability grounds but is not run as part of TSGM's own experiments.

preprint-comprehensive-monitoring-tissue.summary: This preprint introduces NuCLear, a method combining in vivo two-photon imaging of histone 2B-eGFP-labeled cell nuclei with a deep-learning classifier to identify and localize brain cell types (neurons, astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocytes, endothelial cells) non-invasively over time in mouse cortex. To balance the number of training examples across cell types, the authors used the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) package to generate synthetic nuclei feature datasets exploiting correlations, means, extrema and standard deviations of the original features, achieving about 83% fidelity to the original data distribution.

preprint-learning-antidote-individual-un.summary: This paper proposes a method to remedy individual unfairness in machine learning by learning and generating 'antidote data' that stays on the true data manifold, used either as a pre-processing augmentation or combined with a Distributionally Robust Optimization in-processing objective, and demonstrates minimal utility cost across multiple tabular datasets. For continuous feature encoding, the authors adopt CTGAN's mode-specific normalization technique in their own generative model and inherit its hyperparameters, citing CTGAN as the source of this technique rather than running the SDV library itself.
preprint-learning-antidote-individual-un.needs: Unclear whether the inherited hyperparameters reflect actual CTGAN code execution or just borrowed configuration values for their own reimplementation; treated as citation_only/adopted-not-run given no evidence of running the sdv-dev package.

preprint-deep-generative-modeling-econom.summary: A working paper exploring deep generative modeling techniques applied to public procurement data in economics, discussing how such models can address data imbalance and discrete-valued inputs. The authors describe several generative approaches from the literature rather than presenting a benchmark of running libraries. CTGAN is cited descriptively as a framework for handling imbalanced, discrete tabular data, with its procedure referenced but not shown to be run in the available evidence.
preprint-deep-generative-modeling-econom.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was actually run on the procurement data or only discussed as prior art.

preprint-discriminator-class-conditional.summary: This paper proposes BCT-GAN, a bi-discriminator conditional GAN for synthesizing heterogeneous tabular data with continuous, binary, and discrete columns, introducing a novel conditional term based on the chi-squared distribution and dual discriminator architecture to give the generator richer gradient information. It is explicitly built on top of CT-GAN's design, adapting its variational Gaussian mixture preprocessing and conditional vector/training-by-sampling scheme, and is evaluated against CT-GAN and other baselines on four public benchmark datasets using likelihood fitness and machine learning efficacy metrics. CTGAN's conditional generator, mode-specific normalization, and training-by-sampling design are extended into this new bi-discriminator architecture, with CT-GAN also run as a comparison baseline.

paper-causal-tgan-2021.summary: Introduces Causal-TGAN, a tabular generator that conditions generation on a causal graph over the columns so that samples follow the causal structure rather than the joint distribution alone, and reports performance close to the strongest baseline while requiring only a partial graph. CTGAN is the leading comparison generator, its Gaussian-mixture encoding of continuous columns is adopted for every model in the study, and all reported metrics are computed with the SDV package's single-table evaluation module.

preprint-minority-class-oversampling-tab.summary: This paper studies deep generative models (GANs and VAEs, including the authors' own proposals) for oversampling minority classes in imbalanced tabular classification tasks, running a large-scale evaluation (160K+ experiments) comparing these methods against SMOTE-style baselines across sampling ratios. The authors note improvements are often minor relative to effort and that undersampling drives much of the gain. CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) appears only in the reference list, cited as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, with no evidence it was run or engaged with in the body text.

paper-anonymisation-groundhog-day-2020.summary: Measures the privacy gain of publishing synthetic data by running the same linkage and attribute-inference games against synthetic datasets and against traditionally sanitised releases, and concludes that synthetic data either fails to stop the attacks or loses the utility it was meant to preserve, with the gain varying so widely from record to record that it cannot be promised in advance. CTGAN is one of the five generative models the attacks are run against, and is the deep tabular generator carried through the headline per-record results.

paper-insurance-datasets-ctgan-2019.summary: Argues that actuarial research is held back by the absence of realistic public datasets, and builds a workflow that synthesizes shareable insurance data from restricted sources. CTGAN is the generator that workflow is built around, an early application of the architecture to a field whose data almost never leaves the firm that holds it.

thesis-generative-adversarial-networks-l.summary: This PhD dissertation develops deep generative model-based frameworks—GAN variants incorporating fusion strategies and Bayesian uncertainty estimation—for classifying and imputing missing values in longitudinal/time-series data, validated on real-world healthcare and education datasets. The work surveys GAN-based approaches to longitudinal data imputation and proposes three novel frameworks (FaIC-GAN, BaLI-GAN, and related models) that outperform existing baselines on incomplete, heterogeneous data. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) appears only as a bibliography entry among hundreds of references on generative models for tabular/sequential data, with no discussion or use in the body text.
